channel.title: PostKina — Stories worth sharing
channel.description: Source-led reporting and original context for Europe and the wider world.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Europe Briefing: Unrest in France and Albania, Ukraine Intelligence, Russian Recruitment
item.description: Developments across Europe include ongoing unrest in France and Albania, questions surrounding Ukraine's intelligence sharing with the US, and reports of Russian recruitment tactics.

item.title: Zelensky in Oslo for Talks Amidst Intelligence Dispute
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with US envoys in Oslo, Norway, as a dispute emerged over the alleged withholding of critical intelligence by the United States.

item.title: Arson Suspect Detained After Historic Limoges Town Hall Fire
item.description: A fire, suspected to be arson, has caused significant damage to the historic town hall in Limoges, France, leading to the collapse of its clock tower spire.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Geopolitical Tensions, Social Unrest, and Public Figures in Focus
item.description: Ukraine raises concerns over US intelligence sharing, Italy and Albania grapple with violent protests, Pope Leo XIV makes a public appearance post-surgery, and tennis star Elina Svitolina discusses the personal impact of the war.

item.title: Catalonia's Puigdemont Cleared for Return to Spain After Court Ruling
item.description: Carles Puigdemont, Catalonia's former president, is now able to return to Spain after a court upheld a decision to lift the arrest warrant against him. The warrant stemmed from his leadership of the 2017 independence bid.

item.title: EU Steel Tariffs Inadvertently Hamper Ukraine's Vital Industry, Says Metinvest CEO
item.description: European Union tariffs, designed to curb cheap steel imports from countries like China, are inadvertently impacting Ukraine's crucial steel industry, according to Metinvest CEO Yuriy Ryzhenkov. This situation poses a significant economic challenge for Ukraine amidst ongoing conflict and reconstruction efforts, testing the coherence of EU support.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: France Riots, US-Russia Sanctions Eased, Anti-Putin Sabotage, Bomb Threat
item.description: France grapples with unrest, US suspends Russia sanctions, reports of internal sabotage emerge, and a flight faces a bomb threat.

item.title: Western Nations Deport Russian Dissidents Amid Rising Trend
item.description: A concerning trend has emerged over the past year, with a notable increase in anti-government activists from Russia being deported from European Union and United States territories back to Russia, despite seeking refuge in the West.

item.title: France Confronts Aftermath of Widespread Riots and Looting
item.description: France is grappling with the extensive fallout from nationwide protests that escalated into riots and looting, resulting in significant property damage and nearly 1,800 arrests. The unrest, marked by burnt-out vehicles and shattered glass, has prompted urgent calls for calm and a reassessment of public order strategies across the country.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Unrest in France and Albania, Cross-Border Crime, and Ukraine's Starlink Concerns
item.description: Europe grapples with widespread civil unrest in France and Albania, a cross-border murder plot involving a Norwegian teen, and critical questions surrounding Ukraine's access to the Starlink network amid Russian attacks.

item.title: Pope Francis Discharged After Lung Cancer Surgery, Set for Sunday Angelus
item.description: Pope Francis has been discharged from hospital days after lung cancer surgery and is scheduled to deliver the traditional Angelus prayer in St Peter's Square on Sunday. His swift return to public duties underscores the global significance of his health and the demanding nature of his role.

item.title: The Hortensia Diamond: A Century's Return to Public View After Apple Heist
item.description: The historic Hortensia diamond, a rare pink gem and a jewel of the French Crown, is once again on public display in France. This marks its first public exhibition since its dramatic recovery a century ago, following a peculiar 1926 theft where it was found hidden inside an apple. The event reintroduces a captivating piece of European royal history to a new generation.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Europe Briefing: US Sanctions Shift, Ukraine Offensive, German Spy Trial, Papal Health
item.description: US President Trump waives Russia sanctions, impacting Ukraine's fight. Italy criticizes the move. A German spy scandal trial continues, and the Pope is pictured post-surgery.

item.title: EU Leaders Back Ukraine's Right to Self-Defense Amidst Trump Criticism
item.description: European leaders have reaffirmed Ukraine's right to self-defense following Donald Trump's controversial remarks, which questioned President Zelenskyy's cooperation and labeled recent strikes a "disgrace."

item.title: French Prime Minister Alleges Manipulation of Student Protests Ahead of Presidential Election
item.description: France's political landscape is heating up as student protests draw accusations of manipulation from the Prime Minister, who suggests their anger is being weaponised to influence the upcoming presidential election. Unions are poised to join the demonstrations, raising concerns about potential social unrest and the integrity of the electoral process.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Bus Collides with Stationary Train Near French Channel Tunnel Entrance
item.description: A bus crashed into a stationary train on the French side of the Channel Tunnel, causing 19 injuries.

item.title: Azerbaijan's School Headscarf Ban Ignites Rare Protests and Diplomatic Row with Turkey
item.description: A new policy banning headscarves in Azerbaijani schools has led to uncommon domestic protests and a diplomatic dispute with Turkey.

item.title: Ukraine Resumes Strikes on Russian Energy Sites Amid Refinery Accusations
item.description: Kyiv signals a shift in strategy, targeting Russian energy infrastructure amid competing claims.

item.title: MI5 Chief Warns of Escalating State and AI Threats to UK Security
item.description: The MI5 chief warns about evolving state threats and emerging risks involving artificial intelligence.
